locator.text: Display 35.1, p. 35, in the statement of Lemma 4.8

evidence: paper: T_d = e^{M_d} + 10, \qquad P_* > e^{T_d}, \qquad 0 < h < \min\{1/100,\ \lambda,\ e^{-T_d}\}.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. The three conditions are not one Lean statement; they are a definition and two thresholds, and each Lean condition implies the paper's. (a) T_d is literally `Parameters.dropLength c = Real.exp c.m + 10`, identical. (b) In place of P_* > e^{T_d} the Lean imposes `amplitudeThreshold m = Real.exp (Real.exp m + 11) + 1 ≤ P`, i.e. P ≥ e^{T_d+1} + 1 > e^{T_d}; this is the value actually chosen at PreparedOutgoing.lean:39 (max 2 (amplitudeThreshold M)). (c) In place of 0 < h < min{1/100, λ, e^{-T_d}} the Lean imposes 0 < h (TailData.h_pos), 2h < λ (TailData.h_small) and h ≤ heightThreshold m λ = min(1/100, λ/4, e^{-(T_d+2+3/5)}/8); each of λ/4 < λ and e^{-(T_d+13/5)}/8 < e^{-T_d} is the tighter bound, so the paper's display holds a fortiori. Since Lemma 4.8 asserts the existence of parameters meeting these conditions, the tighter Lean conditions give the paper's display; nothing of the display is missing. Note that the lower bound on P is imposed only where the cone clauses (iii) need it: the profile construction itself (ScheduledProfileChoice.exists_scheduled_core_below, L20-28) assumes only 0 < P.
